summary:
Geo-Detective is a web app that lets anyone investigate real-world environmental questions using NASA Earth science data. 
In this application, people are provided with interactive charts and maps, highlighting environmental changes, significant trends, and potential relationships, so regional differences and opposing trends are easy to spot.
It matters because choosing the right variables and datasets is a big barrier for students, researchers, and the public. Geo-Detective cuts down on time and expertise, supports evidence-based exploration, and keeps interpretation honest by flagging the limits of correlation.
details:
Geo-Detective is a web application that helps users investigate real-world environmental questions using NASA Earth science data. Users select an investigation type (Trend, Relationship, or Explanation), enter their question, and specify the variables, geographic region, and time period. The application identifies relevant NASA datasets, retrieves the data, and applies statistical methods such as trend analysis, p-values, and correlation analysis. The project presents results through interactive charts and maps, highlighting environmental changes, significant trends, and potential relationships.

The project makes NASA’s scientific data more accessible and easier to understand. It reduces the time and technical knowledge required to find suitable datasets, helping students, researchers, and the public explore environmental challenges and make evidence-based discoveries. It aims to encourage scientific curiosity and support better-informed environmental awareness and decision-making.

We used web development technologies, including Next.js, JavaScript, CSS, and Python-based statistical analysis, alongside NASA’s Earth science data services and metadata catalogue.

We considered scientific accuracy, data availability, statistical significance, usability, geographic coverage, time resolution, and the limitations of interpreting correlations.
